_comment: The road itself. Each LEG has two or more ROUTES you can swap between — for weather, for closures, or just for what you feel like. Waypoints are real lat/lon, dense enough that the polyline through them approximates true road distance (the app applies a 1.04 wiggle factor). Mileage, day splits and every stop's position are recomputed from this, so edit freely. 'risk' marks winter trouble; 'elev' is feet.

vehicle.name: 2023 Honda Accord Hybrid EX-L
vehicle.chainRule: FWD does NOT qualify for California's R2 exemption, which is 4WD/AWD only. Under R2 this car needs chains ON. Carry low-clearance cable-style devices sized to the sidewall — check the owner's manual for Honda's chain clearance restriction before buying.
vehicle.note: Low ground clearance and touring all-seasons. This is a car that should not be on a mountain interstate during a storm regardless of what's in the trunk.

routes.name: The Route 66 road
routes.character: The great one. Everything worth seeing between here and Memphis is strung along it.
routes.why: The Grand Canyon, Meteor Crater, the Painted Desert and 1,500 miles of old Route 66. If the weather cooperates there is no argument for taking anything else.
routes.costs: Two genuine winter obstacles — Flagstaff at 6,900 feet and the Panhandle ice belt.

routes.name: The southern line
routes.road: I-40 to Nashville, then I-24, I-75 and I-85
routes.character: Same road as far as Nashville, then it drops around the Smokies instead of climbing through them.
routes.why: If Asheville is icing, this trades the mountain crossing for Chattanooga and Atlanta, and picks up the two great aquariums on the way. It lands at the Charlotte end of things, which is where the food is anyway.
routes.costs: Adds about 120 miles over the Asheville road, and you give up the Smokies, Dollywood and downtown Asheville. Monteagle Mountain on I-24 still ices, it is just a shorter climb with more ways around it.

routes.name: The canyon road
routes.road: I-40 to Williams, AZ-64 through the park, US-89 down to Flagstaff
routes.character: Through the canyon instead of out and back to it. You come in at Desert View, take the rim road past Lipan, Moran and Grandview as part of the driving, and leave by the other entrance.
routes.why: The out-and-back from Williams drives the same 60 miles twice. This costs about the same and does not repeat a mile of it, and the Watchtower end is the quiet entrance. It also puts Sunset Crater and Wupatki on the road rather than off it, since US-89 is the way through.
routes.costs: About 130 miles more than staying on I-40, near enough exactly what the out-and-back costs. Higher and more exposed, though: Desert View sits at 7,438 feet and is the first thing to close in weather. If the forecast is bad, take the plain interstate and do the canyon as a spur from Williams, or skip it.

routes.name: The Gulf Coast
routes.character: Down through Atlanta and Montgomery to the water, then west along the coast.
routes.why: New Orleans over New Year's, the Gulf, Mobile, and the Legacy Museum in Montgomery. This is the interesting one.
routes.costs: Slower, and New Orleans on New Year's Eve means booking a room well ahead.

waypoints.name: Atlanta
waypoints.note: Atlanta ices rarely but completely. If a storm is named, wait it out rather than creep through it.

routes.name: The inland run
routes.road: I-85 to Atlanta, I-20 to Marshall, then US-59 south
routes.character: Straight across through Birmingham, Jackson and Dallas.
routes.why: Birmingham's civil rights blocks, Vicksburg, and the cypress trees at Caddo Lake, then straight down US-59 instead of the long way around through Dallas.
routes.costs: Skips New Orleans and the Gulf entirely — which is most of what makes this leg worth doing.

routes.name: The road home
routes.road: I-45 to Dallas, US-287 to Amarillo, then I-40 back
routes.character: Up through Dallas and the empty US-287 corner, then leg 1 in reverse. Everything you skipped going east is still there.
routes.why: Tucumcari's neon works better westbound, Palo Duro is on the way in instead of a backtrack, and the Basque table in Bakersfield is a better last meal than a first one.
routes.costs: The Panhandle and Flagstaff in early January are the same winter problem as leg 1, in reverse order.

routes.name: The Waco line
routes.road: TX-6 through College Station and Waco, then US-287 and I-40
routes.character: The other way from Houston to Dallas, nearly the same distance, through Waco instead of Huntsville.
routes.why: One reason: the mammoths. A nursery herd excavated where it fell, and you walk above the bones. It costs you the Sam Houston statue.
routes.costs: Two-lane Texas highway instead of interstate for the first stretch. Slower per mile, emptier per mile.

routes.name: The Vegas diversion
routes.road: The road home until Kingman, then US-93 north, I-15 south
routes.character: Cut north at Kingman for Hoover Dam and the Strip, come back down to Barstow past Seven Magic Mountains.
routes.why: Ada has never seen anything like the Strip, the dam is free to walk, and the painted boulders are directly on the road out.
routes.costs: Adds roughly 4 hours of driving over staying on I-40, and you give up Oatman's burros on the way through.
